headline: A coalition of AI companies, labor unions and investors is campaigning in Indiana for uniform rules on new data centers and against local moratoriums.
score_reason: Lowered from 5 to 3: the report is from 5 Oct and the pool item is a later republication with nothing new.
importance_line: Communities weighing data-center bans are being offered a common set of rules instead, which could shape state law, but the poll behind the pitch was paid for by the alliance, whose members include data-center developer Digital Realty.
summary: Mirror Indy, with Free Press Indiana News, reports that the American Infrastructure Alliance, a group of 20 organizations including AI companies, unions and investors, has launched a campaign in seven states, including Indiana, for standards such as large power users paying their own electricity costs and enforceable commitments on costs, water use and community benefits. It cites an alliance-funded poll in which support for more data centers in Indiana rises from 19 to 44 percent with the guardrails in place, as at least 24 Indiana counties have passed moratoriums, according to an August Indiana University report.
notes: Credit follows the republication chain (The Republic News, Kokomo Tribune) to Mirror Indy, byline Carson Gerber, 5 Oct 2026. Pool link was The Republic News.
